claim: In the 2011 census Jaisalmer had 17 people per sq km, against 200 for Rajasthan as a whole (less than a tenth; 17.45 unrounded).

evidence.quote: The density of the district is 17 persons per Sq. Km. which is lower than the state density (200 persons per Sq. Km.).

claim: In 2011 Jaisalmer was Rajasthan's largest district by area and the least densely populated of its 33 districts (33rd of 33).

evidence.quote: Jaisalmer district ranks 33rd in terms of population, 1st in terms of area and 33rd in terms of population density.

method: District count: method/compute.py counts 33 district rows in Census A-02 (S03), so 33rd = last. Rajasthan has created new districts since 2011; the rank holds only for 2011 boundaries.

claim: Jaisalmer holds about 11% of Rajasthan's area but under 1% of its people (11.22% vs 0.98%, 2011).

evidence.quote: It shares almost 0.98 percent of state population but 11.22 percent of state area.

claim: Jaisalmer district had 6,69,919 people (about 6.7 lakh) in the 2011 census: sparse, not empty.

evidence.quote: the total population of Jaisalmer district is 669919
The total population of the district is 6,69,919 as per Census, 2011.

claim: Jaisalmer's normal annual rainfall is only about 185 mm (185.5 mm normal; 184.34 mm average for 1901-2006).

evidence.locator: PDF p.26, 'Rainfall' (data credited to DES Rajasthan Statistical Abstract)
evidence.quote: The annual normal rainfall of the district is 185.5 mm.
average annual rainfall in the district during the period 1901 to 2006 works out to be 184.34 mm

claim: Groundwater in Jaisalmer lies as deep as about 124 m below ground (range 0.8 to 124.39 m), and deeper tube wells are often saltier than dug wells in the same village.

evidence.quote: The depth to water level in the district varies from 0.8 mbgl to 124.39 mbgl.
the deeper tube well water has more saline than the dug well water even in same village
There is no perennial river in the district.

claim: Where Jaisalmer is irrigated, most of it is by the Indira Gandhi canal (IGNP): about 61.6% of irrigated area in CGWB's table, the rest from groundwater.

evidence.quote: about 61.61% area is irrigated by canal ( IGNP)
was 58860 hectares; whereas the area irrigated by wells/tube wells was

method: Table 7 recomputed: 210880/342262 = 61.61%. S01 gives 58,860 ha canal vs 42,469 ha wells for 2010-11 (58%); different year and basis, see conflicts.md. Neither source dates CGWB Table 7.

claim: Jaisalmer's population grew almost ninefold between 1901 (75,551) and 2011 (6,69,919), faster than Rajasthan's (about 6.7x).
method: method/compute.py: 669919/75551 = 8.87x; Rajasthan 68548437/10294090 = 6.66x. Boundaries of 1901 recast by the census to 2011 jurisdiction (A-2 convention).

claim: In 2001-2011 Jaisalmer grew 31.81%, faster than Rajasthan's 21.31%.
method: State figure 21.31% from the same table (S03 Rajasthan 2011 row, quoted under C009).

claim: CGWB says groundwater levels are falling even in the canal command areas.

evidence.quote: even in canal command areas water level is declining

claim: The census handbook says Jaisalmer's area is 'almost equal to the state of Kerala' (handbook wording; Kerala's own area not checked in this run).

evidence.quote: almost equal to the state of Kerala

method: Hedged: needs a Kerala area source before narration as a comparison.
